<span id="48d1e81c"></span>
# Background information

When using various types of SDKs to collect and report data, it is necessary to integrate the corresponding SDK in each end first. The subsequent SDK will report the collected data in JSON format. After receiving the reported data, the system will process the JSON data and drop it into the database. The data type after dropping the database is related to the data type in the JSON reported.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Of which:


* Supports the collection and reporting of event and attribute data types must meet the system requirements, otherwise there may be data collection reporting failure, or collection and reporting error but no query results in subsequent query analysis, event and attribute data format requirements see [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

* When integrating the SDK at each end, the system has preset a large number of preset events/properties. You can first understand the existing preset events and properties, and if it does not meet business requirements, you can also create custom events/properties. Preset events/properties are divided into preset event public properties, preset event properties, preset user properties and other types in the use process, and the classification details can be found below [Event/Attribute Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table#3f6c3248).

* The data sources of preset events/properties have different ways, such as obtaining through the system call API, passing in by the user, etc., and the way to close the data collection of preset events/properties from different sources is inconsistent. See below for details [Data sources for events/properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table#007eeb6c).


<span id="3f6c3248"></span>
# Event/Attribute Classification

According to the business data analytics scenario, Finder defines and classifies events and attributes at the following business level for you. Later, when you integrate the SDK and configure event tracking, you can configure the corresponding events/attributes according to your business needs.


|**Event/Attribute Classification** ||**Business Meaning Statement** |
|---|---|---|
|System preset |Preset event public properties |General properties that are reported for each event preset by the system. For example, the device information class field reported by the Finder SDK. |
||Preset events and event properties |System preset event tracking events and event properties. |
||Preset user properties |System\-preset properties that describe the user's own state. |
|Custom |Custom event public properties |Customer\-defined event public properties other than the preset event public properties. |
||Custom events and event properties |Customer\-defined events and event properties other than preset events and event properties. |
||Custom user properties |Customer\-defined user properties other than the preset user properties. |


<span id="007eeb6c"></span>
# Data sources for events/properties


* Data source: Where is the data value of the event/attribute preset by the system obtained from?

* Close collection: refers to whether the SDK automatic collection can be turned off.


See the table below for details.


|**Data source** |**Source Instructions/How to turn off collection** |
|---|---|
|System API |The SDK calls the API method provided by the system to obtain. For the system API type, closing the collection means not calling it. |
|Fixed value |Constants built into the SDK code. For fixed value types, closing means not getting this value. |
|User incoming |The SDK provides methods for users to call incoming. Generally speaking, this type does not support switch control. If you don't want to collect it, you can do it without passing it in. |
|SDK generation |Values generated by SDK native calculations |
|Server level generation |Request the content returned by the server level interface |


<span id="18607162"></span>
# Other event/property descriptions

Due to historical reasons, some attribute names are preceded by "$" and some attribute names are not. There may be attributes with consistent descriptions of attribute meanings, and one attribute name has "$" and one does not have "$". In this case, the actual attribute name and attribute meaning introduction shall prevail.

<span id="6f318cca"></span>
# Preset Attribute Summary Boot Link


* The system presets the Inter\-App communications preset properties any_event and any_active_event for each end, please refer to [Inter-Side Preset Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Inter-Side_Preset_Properties).

* The system presets user attributes for you, and the preset user attributes do not lack the type of access terminal, which is common to all terminals. Please refer to the details [Preset User Properties/Preset Event Public Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_User_Properties_Preset_Event_Public_Properties).

* The preset events/attributes of each end are classified according to the event/attribute, and can be divided into public attributes and event attributes. For a detailed list of each end, please refer to:

   * [Android-Side Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android-Side_Preset_Events_and_Properties)

   * [Web Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_Preset_Events_and_Properties)

   * [Mini Program Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_Preset_Events_and_Properties)

   * [WeChat Official Account Related Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/WeChat_Official_Account_Related_Events_and_Properties)

* In addition:

   * A summary of preset events and properties related to full event tracking for you, see [Full Event Tracking Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Full_Event_Tracking_Preset_Events_and_Properties).

   * A list of properties occupied by the system is summarized for you. You must not create properties with the same name when creating custom properties. See details [Disable Properties List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Disable_Properties_List).
